lines.say: About twenty-three hundred years ago, the Chinese philosopher Zhuangzi wrote down a dream.
shots: archive: Chinese ink painting scholar asleep (Met open access)

lines.say: He dreamed he was a butterfly. Fluttering around, happy, with no idea he was Zhuangzi.
Then he woke up. And there he was, solidly himself again.
shots: q: morning light through paper window

lines.say: But he couldn't settle one question. Was he Zhuangzi, who had dreamed of being a butterfly? Or a butterfly, now dreaming of being Zhuangzi?
shots: line art: butterfly mirrored into scholar outline

lines.say: He left it unanswered. He called it the transformation of things.
Now apply that to death. Every morning, a whole dream world vanishes the second you wake.
What if dying works the same way, and this life is what you wake up from? No one can prove it. No one can rule it out.
